# Exact obstruction to an unrestricted equal-large-partner star bound

Research draft, 6 November 2026. The construction below disproves the proposed assertion that midpoint inclusion and a partner volume at least the middle volume always give some middle point of depth gamma_d(|B|+|A|), even for one pair. It uses d=4 and an exactly equal-volume large partner. It does not refute OC or a star theorem that imposes near-extremal depth on the partner.

## Construction and actual-fiber verification

Let

    T={x in R^4: x_i>=0 and sum_i x_i<=1},
    V=|T|=1/24, g=(1/5,1/5,1/5,1/5),
    t=1/100, epsilon=t^4=1/100000000,
    R=T intersect {x_1,x_2,x_3<=19/100}.

Write lambda_i(x)=x_i for i=1,...,4 and lambda_0(x)=1-sum_i x_i. Inclusion-exclusion of the three coordinate caps gives exactly

    rho:=|R|/V
      =1-3(81/100)^4+3(62/100)^4-(43/100)^4
      =2942511/25000000.

The formula uses the fact that the intersection of any k specified coordinate caps x_i>19/100 is a translated simplex of relative volume (1-19k/100)^4. Here all k<=3 have positive residual height. Proper hyperplane boundaries have zero4-volume, so closed or open versions give the same volume.

Set s=rho^(-1/4)>0, and define

    B=T,
    A=tT+(1-t)g,
    D=sR-(1-t)g.

Then |A|=epsilon V and |D|=s^4|R|=V. Moreover

    (199/100)^4 rho
      =4614561099573711/2500000000000000>1,

so s<199/100=2-t. Since0 in R and R is convex,

    D subset D_big:=(2-t)R-(1-t)g.

Consequently

    (A+D)/2 subset (A+D_big)/2
      =(t/2)T+(1-t/2)R subset T=B.

All bodies are compact convex and full-dimensional. The actual ambient convex body

    K=conv(({-1} x A) union ({0} x B) union ({1} x D))

is full-dimensional in R x R^4 and has integer projection exactly{-1,0,1}. Its endpoint fibers are A and D by extremality of the first coordinate. Its middle fiber is precisely T, since the only new combinations of the endpoints at base0 lie in(A+D)/2 subset T; combinations with the existing middle T also remain in T. Thus these are actual distinct reflected fibers, with |D|=|B| and an arbitrarily specified actual middle center to be tested.

## Universal upper caps and localization of any hypothetical center

Put

    Gamma=gamma_4=256/625,
    Q=Gamma(1+epsilon)=100000001/244140625.

Suppose y in T had raw mixed depth at least QV. This is the proposed star target Gamma(|B|+min(|A|,|D|)).

For any i=0,...,4, choose a closed through-(0,y) ambient halfspace with continuous part lambda_i, and tilt it sufficiently far in the integer coordinate to exclude D completely. The other endpoint contributes at most|A|=epsilon V. Such a finite tilt exists since both endpoint fibers are compact. The middle contribution is the exact simplex cap

    |T intersect {lambda_i>=lambda_i(y)}|
      =(1-lambda_i(y))^4V.

The supposed depth lower bound therefore forces, for every i,

    lambda_i(y)<=1-(Q-epsilon)^(1/4).                    (1)

The exact rational comparison

    Q-epsilon-(7999/10000)^4
      =2047556991999/10000000000000000>0

implies lambda_i(y)<2001/10000 for every i. Since the five barycentric coordinates sum to1, each also satisfies

    lambda_i(y)>1-4(2001/10000)=499/2500.                 (2)

## Three directions that exclude both endpoints

For i=1,2,3, the support bounds are

    max_A lambda_i=t+(1-t)/5,
    max_D lambda_i<=max_D_big lambda_i
                   =(2-t)(19/100)-(1-t)/5.

Their mean is

    [max_A lambda_i+max_D lambda_i]/2
      <=[t+(2-t)(19/100)]/2
       =3881/20000 <499/2500.                            (3)

By(2)-(3), there are thresholds tau_- and tau_+ strictly exceeding the corresponding maxima on A and D and satisfying

    (tau_-+tau_+)/2=lambda_i(y).

For example, add half of the positive gap2lambda_i(y)-max_A lambda_i-max_D lambda_i to each respective maximum. Such thresholds are exactly the restrictions at bases-1 and1 of one through-(0,y) ambient halfspace. That cap therefore excludes both endpoints entirely. Its only mixed mass is the middle simplex cap. The depth assumption now forces

    lambda_i(y)<=1-Q^(1/4), i=1,2,3.                    (4)

For the remaining two indices0,4, retain the weaker bound(1).

## Exact rational incompatibility certificate

Define

    a=80000000199999/100000000000000,
    b=79999999711718/100000000000000.

Direct integer arithmetic gives

    10^56 (Q-a^4)
      =2046464015357401638398208032319760000799999>0,

    10^56 (Q-epsilon-b^4)
      =1532808709965144995626745073502311255197424>0,

    3a+2b-4=23433/100000000000000>0.

Thus3Q^(1/4)+2(Q-epsilon)^(1/4)>4. Summing(4) for the three bad coordinates and(1) for the remaining two yields

    1=sum_i lambda_i(y)
      <=5-3Q^(1/4)-2(Q-epsilon)^(1/4)<1,

a contradiction. No point of the actual middle fiber attains the proposed star target.

All inequalities are exact, and all certifying cuts are actual closed ambient halfspaces. There is no numerical center optimization or unresolved cap formula. The witness s is the specified positive algebraic fourth root; its existence and volume effect are exact.

## What this rules out, and what it leaves intact

This rejects the local bound Gamma(|B|+sum min(|A_i|,|C_i|)) with arbitrary partner shapes even if every relevant partner has volume exactly|B|. The shape or depth restriction in the pending one-sided near-simplex local-star mechanism cannot simply be removed.

For this actual three-fiber source the full sharp-OC target is Gamma(1+epsilon/2)V, which is strictly below the rejected local target Gamma(1+epsilon)V. The construction does not show that this smaller target fails. No claim is made that D has ordinary maximum depth close to Gamma; that is the additional hypothesis supplied by a genuine failed-OC argument when large fibers nearly reach the average mass.

## Explicit partner depth separates this example from the near-extremal regime

For completeness, the equal-volume partner in this example has a definite ordinary depth surplus, and an explicit point in that partner already meets OC. Put c=19/100 and

    h=(c/2,c/2,c/2,(1-3c/2)/2).

Since3c<1, the body R can be written as

    0<=x_1,x_2,x_3<=c, 0<=x_4<=1-x_1-x_2-x_3,

and |R|=c^3(1-3c/2). Its centrally symmetric core S=R intersect(2h-R) has, over a cube point with z=x_1+x_2+x_3, vertical interval

    max(0,3c/2-z)<=x_4<=min(1-z,1-3c/2).

That interval is nonempty because c<1/3. Its volume is

    |S|=|R|-integral_[0,c]^3 |z-3c/2| dx.

Cube reflection about(c/2,c/2,c/2) makes the last integral twice the integral of(3c/2-z)_+. The latter integral is exactly

    [ (3c/2)^4-3(c/2)^4 ]/24=13c^4/64.

One way to verify this elementary integral is to integrate over the positive octant simplex z<=3c/2 and subtract the three regions with one coordinate>c; two such coordinates cannot exceed c in this simplex. Therefore

    |S|=|R|-13c^4/32,
    |S|/(2|R|)=1/2-13c/[64(1-3c/2)]=2041/4576.

Every proper through-h halfspace captures exactly half of the centrally symmetric body S (its hyperplane boundary has zero4-volume), and R contains S. Thus the ordinary normalized depth of h in R is at least2041/4576. Affine covariance gives an actual point sh-(1-t)g in D with ordinary normalized depth at least the same value. In particular,

    D(D)>=2041/4576>256/625=Gamma.

The exact difference is104169/2860000. This definite surplus explains why the construction does not satisfy a sufficiently small near-Grunbaum-depth restriction on the partner. It also exceeds Gamma(1+epsilon/2), so the displayed point at base1 meets the actual sharp-OC target using the partner fiber alone. The star obstruction and this positive certificate concern different allowed locations of the center.
